title: Plan review says "Ready for your approval" over a run whose approval.decide is already committed
description:
FILED BY A FREE AGENT (yaron@cordum.io's standing "improve the UI so it is usable" mandate), 2026-08-27, from a LIVE run of the shipped path at HEAD 52fda230..8bab9211: a real daemon hosting the built bundle, seeded by demo-seed-main.ts, browser paired. Screenshot + full page dump: C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--projexts-moe-next/267e8020-ee4d-4dc9-b5a4-46e4ed922380/scratchpad/shots-after/12-goal-open.png (+ .txt).

THE FALSE STATEMENT, on one screen. The plan-review banner for run-live-1 reads "Ready for your approval" (approve-plan.tsx:108-110 renders it whenever the read answers reviewable:true) while the work board directly beneath it lists `approval.decide @ run-live-1` in the "Already recorded" (COMMITTED) column. The seed transcript confirms: `committed approval.decide demo-seed-approval.decide (effect 9389...)`. Both facts come from the same daemon over the same session; the UI is faithfully rendering two answers that contradict each other.

WHERE THE CONTRADICTION IS PRODUCED (measured, read-only):
- apps/daemon/src/http/planning-run-read.ts:258 - `reviewable: lifecycle === REVIEWABLE_LIFECYCLE`. Reviewability is derived from the run's lifecycle alone. Nothing in that route consults whether a durable approval decision already binds this run.
- The lifecycle evidently stays at PLAN_REVIEW after approval.decide commits (else the banner could not read reviewable:true on this run). Either the approval does not advance the run lifecycle, or the read projects a stale lifecycle - the architect owns finding which.
- The UI half is honest in itself (it prints what the read said), so this is NOT a control-room fix: the read must answer reviewable:false (or a distinct "already decided" state the banner can name) once a decision is durable, or the banner is lying to the human at the one gate that matters most.

WHY A ROW (board filing bar): a correctness defect REACHABLE ON THE SHIPPED PATH - every seeded project reaches this exact state, and once the Approve button is wired (P2.15d family) a human would be invited to approve a run that is already approved. No open row owns planning-run-read.ts's reviewable derivation: task-6646f888 / task-40017f79 build the approval SEAM and the BUTTON, not the read's truth.

NOT IN SCOPE: the plan-review copy itself ("Ready for your approval", the Approve-disabled note) - task-40017f79 owns approve-plan.tsx.
definitionOfDone: POST /planning/run/read answers reviewable:false (or a named already-decided state) for a run that has a durable approval.decide bound to it; proven with a test that commits approval.decide against a sealed run and then reads it, drilled by deleting the approval check and observing the arm red.
A run with NO durable approval still answers reviewable:true with the existing PLAN_REVIEW lifecycle - the positive arm stays green and is asserted in the same test file so the fix cannot flip it.
The live seeded lane (demo-seed-main.ts against a hosted bundle) no longer renders 'Ready for your approval' over a Committed approval.decide; quoted from a fresh page dump, not argued.
taskRails: The UI must keep rendering only what the read answers; no client-side inference from the affordance surface may override the planning read.
Do not touch apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.tsx - task-40017f79 owns it.

implementationPlan.description: Phase 1/2 — VERIFY-OR-BLOCK, zero bytes. THE ROW LEFT ONE QUESTION TO THE ARCHITECT ("Either the approval does not advance the run lifecycle, or the read projects a stale lifecycle") AND IT IS ANSWERED: THE APPROVAL NEVER ADVANCES THE RUN. Measured at HEAD 450ad143 — re-confirm each at yours: (a) `packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-reducer.ts:168-178` is the run reducer's complete command switch and it has NO `approval.decide` case; only `plan.approve` (:66) and `graph.approve` (:68) carry the `["PLAN_REVIEW", "APPROVED"]` transition. (b) `approval.decide` is served by `decideApproval` (planning-services.ts:231-310), whose terminal statement is `return activateInitialGraph(...)`, and that commits `eventType: "GoalExecutionEnabled"` on `aggregateId: input.goalId` — the GOAL aggregate (approval-activation.ts:160-167). It never writes the run aggregate. So the run's lifecycle stays `PLAN_REVIEW` FOREVER after approval.decide, and `planning-run-read.ts:258` `reviewable: lifecycle === REVIEWABLE_LIFECYCLE` (:57 = "PLAN_REVIEW") is therefore true forever. This is NOT a stale projection and NOT a UI fault — do not "fix" the reducer or the lifecycle: adding a transition would change approval semantics far outside this row. (c) THE DURABLE FACT THE READ MUST CONSULT EXISTS: `approval-run-binding.ts:10` states "The daemon's only durable approval fact is `GoalExecutionEnabled`", and TWO production readers already consume it exactly this way — `human-approval-authority-reader.ts:90` (`event.aggregateId === goalRef && event.eventType === "GoalExecutionEnabled"`) and `goal-close-prerequisite.ts:91`. Compose that precedent; invent no new authority. (d) The run record `readPlanningRun` ALREADY loads carries the goal: `planning-services.ts:215` reads `payloadRef(state, "goalRef")` off the same run record, so the read can resolve the goal without a new caller input. (e) Ownership/porcelain: `apps/daemon/src/http/planning-run-read.ts` is CLEAN, 361 lines, and NO planning-run-read test file exists yet; task-40017f79 (WORKING) and task-6646f888 (BLOCKED) mention it in PROSE only — neither declares it in a step file field, as the filer already established. implementationPlan.description: Phase 4 GREEN (reader) — NEW `apps/daemon/src/http/planning-run-approval-binding.ts` plus its REQUIRED sibling bridge `apps/daemon/src/http/planning-run-approval-binding.js` containing exactly `export * from "./planning-run-approval-binding.ts";` (this repo requires the .ts/.js pair; a new module without its bridge typechecks and tests clean while breaking the runtime). Keep it small and single-purpose (≤90 lines): export a function that, given the store, the projectId, the runId and the goalRef already available on the run record, answers whether a durable approval BINDS THIS RUN — by scanning the goal aggregate for `GoalExecutionEnabled` exactly as `human-approval-authority-reader.ts:90` does, and then confirming the event's own binding names this `runId` (approval-activation.ts:91 carries `runId: input.binding.runId` into the durable witness). Distinguish three outcomes with stable codes at its own layer: BOUND (a decision binds this run), ABSENT (no decision), and UNREADABLE (a `GoalExecutionEnabled` exists but its payload will not decode) — UNREADABLE must NEVER be reported as ABSENT, because reporting a corrupt approval as "not approved" is exactly the direction that re-invites a human to approve twice. It is a READ ONLY: no write, no clock, no caller-supplied value.

comments.author: architect-d950bd95
comments.content:
ROOT CAUSE ANSWERED + PLAN SUBMITTED — architect-d950bd95, 2026-08-27 20:00Z, HEAD 450ad143. 6 steps / 4 owned files. The filing left one question to the architect ("Either the approval does not advance the run lifecycle, or the read projects a stale lifecycle — the architect owns finding which"). It is the FIRST branch, and here is the proof.

**`approval.decide` IS NOT A PLANNING-RUN COMMAND AT ALL.** `packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-reducer.ts:168-178` is the run reducer's complete command switch — `planning.ready`, `planning.claim`, `planning.release`, `planning.recover_absent`, `plan.propose`, `planning.finalize_submission`, `plan.approve`, `plan.revise`, `graph.approve`, `goal.cancel` — and there is NO `approval.decide` case. Only `plan.approve` (:66) and `graph.approve` (:68) carry the `["PLAN_REVIEW", "APPROVED"]` transition.

**So where does the approval go?** `decideApproval` (planning-services.ts:231-310) ends at `return activateInitialGraph(...)`, and that commits `eventType: "GoalExecutionEnabled"` on `aggregateId: input.goalId` (approval-activation.ts:160-167) — the GOAL aggregate, never the run. The run's lifecycle therefore stays `PLAN_REVIEW` permanently, and `planning-run-read.ts:258` `reviewable: lifecycle === REVIEWABLE_LIFECYCLE` (:57 = `"PLAN_REVIEW"`) is true forever. Nothing is stale; the read is asking a question that cannot answer this.

**This rules out the tempting fix.** Making `approval.decide` advance the run lifecycle would give a non-run command a run transition and change approval semantics for every consumer of that lifecycle, far outside this row. The plan explicitly forbids it, and drill D4 catches a wiring that overwrites `lifecycle` instead of only `reviewable` — the read must not start lying in the opposite direction, because the run really IS still in PLAN_REVIEW.

**The fix composes a fact that already exists.** `approval-run-binding.ts:10` states outright that "The daemon's only durable approval fact is `GoalExecutionEnabled`", and TWO production readers already consume it exactly this way: `human-approval-authority-reader.ts:90` (`event.aggregateId === goalRef && event.eventType === "GoalExecutionEnabled"`) and `goal-close-prerequisite.ts:91`. No new authority is invented. The inputs are already in hand: the run record `readPlanningRun` loads at :243 carries `goalRef` (planning-services.ts:215 reads `payloadRef(state, "goalRef")` off that same record), and the durable witness carries `runId` (approval-activation.ts:91) — which is what makes the binding PER-RUN rather than per-goal.

**Two arms that look optional and are not.** ARM 3 (an approval bound to a DIFFERENT run must not flip this run) plus drill D2 exist because a reader that merely asks "does any GoalExecutionEnabled exist on this goal" passes the headline arm while being wrong. And UNREADABLE must never collapse to ABSENT: reporting a corrupt approval as "not approved" is precisely the direction that re-invites a human to approve twice, which is the harm this row exists to stop.

Scope respected: `approve-plan.tsx` is untouched (task-40017f79 owns it) and rail 1 holds — the UI keeps rendering only what the read answers. DoD-3's live seeded-lane proof must be QUOTED from a fresh page dump; if the lane cannot be run, the plan requires disclosing it as unproven rather than substituting the unit arms.
